newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up, movement slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids up, movement slow.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids rose on Tuesday in line with higher Minneapolis spring wheat futures amid sluggish farmer selling, U.S. grain merchandisers said.

"It's still relatively slow, because there are still (railroad) lines that aren't moving," a Minnesota dealer said. Engines from the Dakotas were having trouble pulling cars out of elevators due to a lack of power. But a warming trend was expected next week and could get the grain moving.
In Montana, one merchandiser said recent cold weather delayed December deliveries which had extended into January.
But some wheat was moving this week as the weather improved.
A lack of export news and slow movement were also evident in the Pacific Northwest, an Oregon dealer said.

In export news, the Commodity Credit Corp said it was seeking up to 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 soft white wheat, maximum moisture 13.5 percent, under its export program for Pakistan. Shipment period was February 20 to March 15.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 2-1/4 to four cents per bushel higher, with March up three cents at $3.89-3/4.
